questions.question: Should the day view get dragging too? Right now only the month and week views let you drag, and the docs leave the day view out on purpose because it has only one day to drop on. With a time change added, dragging up and down would make sense there.

options.label: Yes, up and down only (Recommended)
options.description: In the day view you can drag an entry up or down to change its time. The ghost only moves vertically, and the day stays the same.

options.label: No, week view only
options.description: Keep the day view without dragging. Only the week view gets the time change.

result.output: Your questions have been answered: "Should the day view get dragging too? Right now only the month and week views let you drag, and the docs leave the day view out on purpose because it has only one day to drop on. With a time change added, dragging up and down would make sense there."="Yes, up and down only (Recommended)". You can now continue with these answers in mind.

questions.question: When you drop an entry in the hour grid, how should the new start time be worked out?

options.label: Block's top edge, 15-min steps (Recommended)
options.description: The start is wherever the top of the dragged block lands, rounded to the nearest quarter hour. If you grab a 2-hour meeting by its middle, it doesn't jump. The time picker already works in quarter hours.

options.label: Pointer position, 15-min steps
options.description: The start is wherever the pointer is. This is simpler, but the block jumps when you grab it below its top.

options.label: Block's top edge, 30-min steps
options.description: Coarser steps, so it's easier to hit an exact time on a phone.

result.output: Your questions have been answered: "When you drop an entry in the hour grid, how should the new start time be worked out?"="Block's top edge, 15-min steps (Recommended)". You can now continue with these answers in mind.

questions.question: While you drag, should the ghost block show the time it would land on? For example, its "09:00–10:00" would change to "10:15–11:15" as you move it.

options.label: Yes, update the ghost's time (Recommended)
options.description: Without this, landing on 10:15 rather than 10:00 is guesswork, especially on a phone with a 2.4rem hour. It's a small hook in the drag code.

options.label: No, just the column highlight
options.description: This matches how dragging works today. You see the new time after you drop.

result.output: Your questions have been answered: "While you drag, should the ghost block show the time it would land on? For example, its "09:00–10:00" would change to "10:15–11:15" as you move it."="Yes, update the ghost's time (Recommended)". You can now continue with these answers in mind.

questions.question: An entry keeps its length when you move it, so a 1-hour meeting stays 1 hour. What should happen if you drop it low enough that it would run past midnight, for example a 1-hour block dropped at 23:30?

options.label: Clamp: it ends at 24:00 at the latest (Recommended)
options.description: The lowest start allowed is 24:00 minus its length, so the block always stays in the column you dropped it in. Otherwise a late drop would quietly turn it into a multi-day entry and move it to the top strip.

options.label: Allow it to cross midnight
options.description: It becomes a multi-day entry ending the next day and moves up into the top strip.

You can now continue with these answers in mind.

questions.question: What about moving between the top strip (all-day and multi-day entries) and the hour grid?

options.label: No conversion: only the day changes (Recommended)
options.description: This is how it works today. A timed block dropped on the strip only changes its day, and keeps its time. An all-day entry dropped into the hour grid only changes its day and stays all-day. Turning one kind into the other is done in the popup.

options.label: Convert between them
options.description: An all-day entry dropped in the grid becomes a timed entry at that time, 1 hour long. A timed block dropped on the strip becomes all-day. This needs more rules, e.g. what happens to a timed multi-day entry.

#!/bin/bash
# Runs the model checks in node, then starts the fixture server and a headless Chromium for the
# browser checks and tears both down.
#
#   test/run.sh              every check
#   test/run.sh --shot DIR   every check, and a screenshot of each view into DIR
#   test/run.sh mine         one app's browser checks, by the name in test/check-<app>.mjs
#
# Needs chromium and node 20+ on PATH. Nothing is installed and nothing is written to the repo.
#
# A browser suite per app, discovered rather than listed: adding test/check-diary.mjs is all it
# takes for the diary to be checked by this script. They share one Chromium and run in turn,
# because they drive the same page target.
set -u
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
PORT=8787
PROFILE=$(mktemp -d)

cleanup() {
  [ -n "${CHROME:-}" ] && kill "$CHROME" 2>/dev/null
  [ -n "${SERVER:-}" ] && kill "$SERVER" 2>/dev/null
  rm -rf "$PROFILE" 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}
trap cleanup EXIT

command -v chromium >/dev/null || { echo "chromium not on PATH"; exit 2; }

# A bare word is an app name; everything else is passed to the suites.
ONLY=""
ARGS=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --shot) ARGS+=("$1" "$2"); shift 2 ;;
    -*) ARGS+=("$1"); shift ;;
    *) ONLY="$1"; shift ;;
  esac
done

content.text:
Both changes are in and the full `test/run.sh` passes. Nothing is committed yet.

**Dragging a block to a new time (week and day views)**
- **How it works:** in the hour grid, a timed block now takes the time its top edge lands on, rounded to 15 minutes. It keeps its length, and if dropped too low it starts as late as still ends at 24:00 rather than running into the next day.
- **While dragging:** the dragged copy shows the time it would land on (e.g. `10:15–11:15`).
- **Day view:** dragging is new here, and moves a block up and down only; the copy can't drift sideways.
- **Unchanged:**
  - The month view still changes only the day.
  - A repeating entry still moves just that one occurrence.
  - A timed block dropped on the top strip changes only its day.
  - An all-day entry dropped in the hour grid changes only its day.
- **Code:** `moveToDay` in `calendar/data.js` takes an optional minute-of-day. `calendar/drag.js` gets an `over(ghost, target)` hook, called as the copy moves, and `axis` can now be a function. The logic is in `wireDrag` in `calendar/views.js`.

**Long titles widening the week**
The cause was the week grid's columns (`1fr`), which can't get narrower than their content. A long multi-day or all-day title in the top strip widened its day and pushed the week past the right edge. The columns are now `minmax(0, 1fr)`, so titles get the ellipsis they already had. This is a one-line change in `calendar/style.css`. A screenshot of the week at 360px shows equal columns.

**Tests**
- **Overflow:** a new check at 360px confirms no top-strip cell is wider than its day's column. It fails on the old CSS on 15 days across those weeks, and passes now.
- **Old week test:** it said a block "keeps its time wherever in the column it lands". I replaced it with three new checks:
  - In the week, a block lands 2 hours later in the next column, with the same length.
  - On a phone in the day view: the copy stays in its column and shows the time it would land on, and the block lands an hour earlier.
  - Dropped at the bottom of the day, a block ends at midnight and stays in the hour grid.

**Docs and cache:** I rewrote the drag rule in `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md`, which said the opposite, and added a rule about cut-short strip titles. `calendar/TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` and `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` are updated to match, and the `sw.js` cache version is bumped.

**Left as is:** in the narrow week strip, an entry's time (e.g. `→07:00`) can take the whole cell and leave no room for the title.
